findings.title: TagDevice now runs synchronously on request path, blocking auth flow
findings.body: The previous implementation ran anonDeviceService.TagDevice in a background goroutine with a timeout context, decoupling the DB write from the authentication request. The change removed the goroutine and now calls TagDevice synchronously using ctx from the request. Every anonymous request now blocks on a DB write (CreateOrUpdateDevice/updateDevice) before returning the identity, which can meaningfully increase latency and DB load for anonymous auth, especially under high traffic. This also means any DB slowness/timeouts directly affect user-facing anonymous request latency, not just background error logging.

findings.title: Device limit reached blocks ALL anonymous authentication, not just the specific device
findings.body: When ErrDeviceLimitReached is returned from TagDevice, Authenticate now returns (nil, err), causing authentication to fail entirely for the anonymous client. Previously, tagging failures were just logged as warnings and the anonymous identity was still returned. Now, once the device limit is reached, any new anonymous device/session will fail to authenticate at all (since Test() always returns true and there's no fallback), effectively breaking anonymous access for all new devices once the configured limit is hit, rather than just skipping the quota tracking as likely intended.

findings.title: Device limit check has a race condition (count-then-insert without transaction)
findings.body: In CreateOrUpdateDevice, the device limit is enforced by first running a separate CountDevices query and only then performing the insert/upsert in a different statement. Between the count and the insert, concurrent requests can also pass the same check, allowing the device limit to be exceeded under concurrent load. This is a classic TOCTOU race since there is no transaction or locking tying the count and insert together.

findings.title: New device_limit setting not documented
findings.body: A new ini configuration key `device_limit` is added under `[auth.anonymous]` (cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit), but there is no accompanying update to configuration documentation (e.g., conf/defaults.ini, docs/sources/setup-grafana/configure-grafana) in the diff. Users have no way to discover this new setting or its default/behavior without reading the source.
